scientific_question: Starting from the exact trained Native CLM v0 M1 checkpoint, can protected sparse Cell-local updates learn sequential language distributions without learner-side replay while retaining prior language behavior better than unsafe writes?
formal_seed_policy: formal seeds must remain untouched until the frozen protocol is run

registered_mechanism.optimizer: fresh AdamW at each phase; optimizer state is not carried across domain boundaries
registered_mechanism.protected_arm: Cell gradients projected through certificate nullspace before optimizer step
registered_mechanism.unsafe_arm: identical Cell-local write stream with certificate projection disabled
registered_mechanism.certificate_updates: both arms continue the same registered periodic certificate update mechanism
registered_mechanism.reason_for_freezing_router: routing inputs occur before Cell execution; freezing shared/router makes protected and unsafe arms share the same read-address geometry, isolating write protection

two_gpu_execution.rationale: the 12.15M model is too small to benefit materially from DDP; independent arms avoid gradient synchronization and approximately halve wall-clock time for the registered causal comparison
two_gpu_execution.formal_schedule: for each formal seed, run protected and unsafe concurrently; seeds execute sequentially

claim_boundary: This is real token-predictive continual-language training, not a synthetic operator world.
The M1 shared substrate and learned router are frozen in M2 to isolate Cell-local write protection.
M2 does not test autonomous growth, learned topology change, router continual adaptation, Dense/MoE superiority, or language-scale asymptotics.
A negative result is preserved and advances the diagnosis to capacity/protection limits rather than being retuned on formal seeds.
